$comment: Generated by scripts/ai-readiness/build-trap-index.mjs. `disposition`, `gate`, `supersededBy` and `provenance` are HAND-OWNED and carried forward on every rebuild; everything else is re-derived from the skills and the eval fixtures. `evaluated` is derived from `coveredBy` and must never be hand-written. The counts below are a GAP REPORT, not a score — driving `open` down by deleting traps instead of gating them is the failure this file exists to make visible.

dispositions.open: prose only — nothing but a reading agent checks this
dispositions.evaluated: an eval case cites it; the wrong answer is possible but scored
dispositions.gated: a script refuses the wrong answer outright, so the prose is a backstop
dispositions.superseded: the trap was wrong or its cause was removed; `supersededBy` says what replaced it

traps.title: Opacity is a PERCENTAGE, and a value comparison PASSES when the canvas is broken
traps.provenance: Measured live 2026-08-27 on al-field-note State=Disabled: stored 0.4 → node.opacity === 0.004 (invisible); stored 40 → 0.4 (correct). The trap flipped the repo's own docs TWICE, because the stored-value check (0.4 === 0.4) passes precisely when the canvas is broken. The fraction-enforcing setValue calls in scripts/figma-var-fixes.mjs were removed 2026-08-27. Restated at altitude-figma-sync#5.

traps.title: Recolour must not be gated behind glyph resolution
traps.provenance: Presented as 'the chip\'s close icon is the wrong colour'. The nested-icon branch in build-set-code.mjs ran swapComponent AND the recolour inside one `if (glyphName && nestedGlyphByName[glyphName])`, so a failed Phosphor lookup left the wrapper instance in place with its cached PaperPlaneTilt glyph and a hardcoded white fill.

traps.provenance: A Phosphor icon instance ships the real shapes PLUS one VECTOR the size of the icon box (16x16 for a 16px icon); painting every vector fills that box solid and the glyph reads as a knocked-out silhouette.

traps.title: --refresh materialises half-landed changes into a gate failure
traps.provenance: emit-contracts.mjs grew a layout.wrap anatomy fact that contract.schema.json had never been taught to allow. Nothing failed while the contracts on disk predated the change; the first --refresh wrote wrap into 7 contracts and --check went red, while --check-drift stayed green throughout because disk and derivation agreed — they were just both invalid.

traps.title: Two sets on one page can share a NAME — and the tools then disagree
traps.provenance: 2026-08-27: eight 🛠 pages carried the owner's hand-built reference set AND the generated set under the same name (e.g. `List Item`), and 14 more still had the collision. The generated sets were also the broken ones — al-list-item's had zero padding, unbound pure-black text (invisible in dark mode) and 3 of 6 states. The artifact that exposed the disagreement was the prop sheet, retired 2026-08-29; the collision it exposed is still live.

traps.title: The contract can UNDER- and OVER-state the variant matrix
traps.provenance: Both directions were live. UNDER: eight components' sets were missing states their reference sets had, because a state reaches the contract only with a measured stateOverride or an SCSS delta. OVER: al-progress's Shape=Bar × Size=Lg|Md|Xl were never measured (circleSize only applies when isCircle) — 6 phantom variants pruned. While the prop sheet existed, regenerating the grid dropped the states you had just restored and failed on the phantoms you had just pruned with `setProperties: Unable to find a variant with those property values`.

traps.title: A width: 100% component measures ZERO WIDE
traps.provenance: al-progress's bar is width: 100% (progress.scss:15,26); in an unconstrained harness its track measured {w: 0, h: 4} and generation produced an empty 100x100 frame with no children. Its intrinsically-sized circle generated fine. Repair bindings: --al-theme-color-background-neutral-strong for the track, --al-theme-color-content-primary-default for the fill.

traps.title: "The Figma set has no padding" is usually a MEASUREMENT bug, not a Figma bug
traps.provenance: Until 2026-08-27 measure-lib.js's PROPS list held only the physical padding longhands, while 27 components author LOGICAL ones — 64 declarations, every one invisible to the contract, so those components generated with no padding at all. al-list-item was the proof: list-item.scss:43-46 sets padding-block-start, and its contract's link node bound font, letter-spacing and width and nothing else. Fixed by adding the logical names to PROPS and folding them onto the physical sides in expand().

traps.provenance: The original trap read: "Never force an auto-layout onto a root that is not flex in the browser. Defaulting to HORIZONTAL laid al-tabs' tablist and its panel side by side — 557x40 against a real 291x79. Non-flex roots keep their measured absolute geometry." The symptom was real; the diagnosis and the fix were both wrong, and the last sentence is false. Measured live on al-table: root frame 243px wide inside a 100x100 component, the run reporting maxVariantWidth/Height 100. The bug was live on 327 nodes across 53 of 103 components until 2026-08-27. After the fix al-tabs is VERTICAL — al-c-tabs__header at y0, al-c-tabs__body at y36, component 426x168, zero overflow. THIS ENTRY IS THE REASON THE LIFECYCLE EXISTS: it was marked SUPERSEDED by hand and nothing but a cross-session mailbox message noticed.
